states.normal: device in service; the attacker holds remote and local protocol access only, and no bench access to headers, test pads or the boot strap
states.temporary-physical-possession: attacker holds the device on a bench: case open, SWD header and test pads reachable, UART console reachable, boot strap for ROM download reachable
states.authenticated-recovery: the explicitly authenticated recovery path has been entered; it is a separately authorized state, not an ordinary run state and not a rollback bypass

interfaceAttempts.tokenGrammar: Each entry of DeviceConfig.interfaces[<surface>] is a complete statement of that surface’s authority in one possession state, written as <state>:<surface>:<authority>. A bound authority (…:no-unrestricted-readout, …:console-log-only, …:authenticated-image-download-only) states what the surface may not do beyond the named limit; a capability authority (…:recovery-session, …:recovery-console, …:recovery-image-download) states the only action that remains. interfaceCan(config, surface, token) answers whether that authority statement is part of production policy for the surface.

policyAuthorities.meaning: in normal service SWD holds no unrestricted firmware or secret readout authority; no general debug session is enumerated
with the board on a bench SWD still holds no unrestricted firmware or secret readout authority: temporary physical possession does not escalate SWD authority
the explicitly authenticated recovery session is the only SWD authority that remains; it drives the recovery path and carries no readout authority
in normal service the UART console emits log output only: no command shell, no image install, no secret readout
with the console reachable on a bench it still emits log output only: possession does not escalate console authority
the authenticated recovery console is the only UART authority that remains
in normal service the ROM download path holds no authority: the mode is not reachable without the boot strap and no image write path is open

with the boot strap reachable, ROM download accepts only images that pass the same integrity, product and rollback gate the bootloader applies (see downloadGate); it cannot lower rollback state and is not a flash readout path
ROM download inside the authenticated recovery path accepts only the authorized recovery image

totals.writePathNote: the only authorized write-path attempts are the two bounded download authorities; each is limited by downloadGate, and every rollback-state-clear and unauthorized image-install attempt is denied

derivation: product device-x and production key hash prod-key-hash-2026 are the corpus values, so the gate is bound to this product and this board's key-hash fuse record
minimumVersion 7 is the version of the board-observed current image (current@7), so no image older than the deployed one is accepted
bootloaderVerifiesSignature and bootloaderVerifiesProduct are enabled so the unsigned and wrong-product fixtures reject before execution
rollbackStateProtected is enabled so version state cannot be lowered by an ordinary firmware write
recoveryRequiresAuthorization is enabled, and debugFuseObserved is false because the corpus records emulator.debugLockProof=false
downloadGate.purpose: Every interface write path, including ROM USB download and the authenticated recovery path, is bounded by this gate. Interface authority is therefore never broader than the boot policy: "download permitted" can only ever mean "download permitted for an image this gate accepts".

recoveryDemonstration.claimUnderTest: recovery is a separately authorized destination, not a signature-only rollback bypass, and a failed recovery never lands in an unverified slot

withAuthorization.note: the supplied recovery image carries its separate authorization and is below the minimum version, so it is accepted only through the recovery destination

counterfactualWithoutAuthorization.note: derived counterfactual: the same signed, non-corrupt, correctly bound image with the separate authorization removed is rejected as a rollback, which is what makes recovery an authorization rather than a bypass

withAuthenticatedCandidate.note: an authenticated production image is installed and committed from authorized recovery; a pre-commit cut keeps the device in authorized recovery

withUnsignedCandidate.note: a failed restore from authorized recovery leaves the device in an authenticated state rather than on an unverified slot

recoveryDemonstration.conclusion: The recovery condition is demonstrated, not assumed: the same signed image enters recovery only with its separate authorization, is rejected as a rollback without it, and no power-cut step from authorized recovery selects an unverified slot.

supportedByThisArtifact: the production lock register is observed on the representative board (corpus.observed.productionLockRegister=true), and the fixture contract states its semantics: swdReadoutLocked=true, authorizedRecoveryOnly=true

SWD holds no unrestricted firmware or secret readout authority in normal service or under temporary physical possession, and its only remaining authority is the explicitly authenticated recovery session
UART is bounded to console log output and ROM USB download to authenticated images in both states, so temporary physical possession does not escalate interface authority
ROM download authority is bounded by the same gate the bootloader applies: older@5 -> reject-rollback, unsigned@8 -> reject-signature, wrong-product@8 -> reject-product, corrupt@8 -> reject-corrupt

recovery is separately authorized: removing the authorization turns the same signed recovery image into a rollback rejection, and every power-cut step from authorized recovery lands in an authenticated slot

the credential lifecycle contract is exercised end to end by the authored model: provision, use, rotate, revoke, reset, RMA, decommission, and the reset/recovered device cannot regain authorization silently while its fleet entry is revoked
notEstablished: debug lock effectiveness: corpus.emulator.debugLockProof=false, and the production lock register is a different register whose semantics come from the fixture contract
resistance to invasive extraction and fault injection: invasiveResistanceClaimed=false, faultInjectionResistanceClaimed=false; neither was exercised
credential hardware behaviour: no credential, key-slot or fleet observation exists in the corpus, so every credential result is documentation/simulation

communications and peripheral behaviour (BLE/Wi-Fi provisioning, NFC, removable media, DMA-capable peripherals, hidden service protocols, manufacturing commands): no observation exists in this fixture
claims.claimBoundary: This artifact shows interface-authority policy, the boot/update gate that bounds every write path, and the credential lifecycle state machine. It does not show debug lock, fuse enforcement, physical secret-extraction resistance, fault-injection resistance or real flash behaviour; those need representative hardware.

limits: The supplied simulator models boot, update and recovery decisions. It has no credential, fleet, RMA or decommission state, so the credential lifecycle is an authored model (scripts/device-lifecycle-model.ts) and every one of its results is documentation/simulation.
The corpus records no credential, key-slot or fleet observation, so nothing in the credential lifecycle is hardware-observed.

The corpus records emulator.physicalFuseProof=false and emulator.debugLockProof=false, so invasive-extraction and fault-injection resistance stay unclaimed and the effective debug lock is not proven here.
Image digests are content digests of the corpus image records, not measurements of flash contents on hardware.
The recovery counterfactual, the update candidates and the unsigned candidate are derived fixtures: they are labelled as such and are not present in evidence/device-corpus.json.
Interface authority is evaluated as policy membership through interfaceCan; the fixture supplies no board observation of an interface attempt, so no attempt result is hardware-observed.
Communications, peripherals and safety consequences are recorded as requirements in .kory-eval/threat-model.md; this fixture supplies no observation for any of them.
